Generate synthetic data for a stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial

Source: R/mock-designs.R
mock_stepped_wedge.Rd

Produces one row per participant per period, with clusters nested within sites. Each cluster is assigned a crossover sequence – the period in which it switches from control to intervention – and every cluster eventually receives the intervention (the defining feature of a stepped wedge). The arm for a given participant-period row is derived from whether the current period has reached the cluster's sequence (period >= sequence), so treatment assignment is genuinely driven by the roll-out schedule rather than an unused column.

Usage

mock_stepped_wedge(
  n_clusters = 12L,
  n_participants = 480L,
  n_periods = 4L,
  n_sites = 3L,
  arm_labels = c("Control", "Intervention"),
  seed = 123L
)

Arguments

n_clusters

Integer. Number of clusters.

n_participants

Integer. Total number of participants (each contributes one row per period), distributed unevenly across clusters.

n_periods

Integer. Number of periods, including the initial all-control period. Must be >= 2 (clusters need at least one period before crossover and one after).

n_sites

Integer. Number of sites (clusters nested in sites; must be <= n_clusters).

arm_labels

Character vector of length 2: c(control_label, intervention_label).

seed

Integer. Random seed for reproducibility.

Value

A tibble::tibble() with one row per participant per period, including participant_id, event_id, cluster_id, site_id, period, sequence, arm (derived from period >= sequence), demographic columns, and consent-flow columns.

See also

Other mock data: mock_cluster_rct(), mock_crossover(), mock_parallel_rct()

Examples

mock_stepped_wedge()
#> # A tibble: 1,920 × 15
#>    participant_id event_id cluster_id site_id period sequence arm            age
#>    <chr>          <chr>    <chr>      <chr>    <int>    <int> <chr>        <dbl>
#>  1 P0001          E00001   C07        S2           1        2 Control         37
#>  2 P0001          E00002   C07        S2           2        2 Intervention    37
#>  3 P0001          E00003   C07        S2           3        2 Intervention    37
#>  4 P0001          E00004   C07        S2           4        2 Intervention    37
#>  5 P0002          E00005   C02        S3           1        3 Control         52
#>  6 P0002          E00006   C02        S3           2        3 Control         52
#>  7 P0002          E00007   C02        S3           3        3 Intervention    52
#>  8 P0002          E00008   C02        S3           4        3 Intervention    52
#>  9 P0003          E00009   C03        S3           1        4 Control         59
#> 10 P0003          E00010   C03        S3           2        4 Control         59
#> # ℹ 1,910 more rows
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: age_group <chr>, sex <chr>, ethnicity <chr>,
#> #   eligible_screen <lgl>, consent_date <date>, baseline_complete <lgl>,
#> #   withdrew <lgl>
mock_stepped_wedge(n_clusters = 8, n_participants = 400, n_periods = 5, seed = 9)
#> # A tibble: 2,000 × 15
#>    participant_id event_id cluster_id site_id period sequence arm            age
#>    <chr>          <chr>    <chr>      <chr>    <int>    <int> <chr>        <dbl>
#>  1 P0001          E00001   C05        S3           1        2 Control         68
#>  2 P0001          E00002   C05        S3           2        2 Intervention    68
#>  3 P0001          E00003   C05        S3           3        2 Intervention    68
#>  4 P0001          E00004   C05        S3           4        2 Intervention    68
#>  5 P0001          E00005   C05        S3           5        2 Intervention    68
#>  6 P0002          E00006   C05        S3           1        2 Control         41
#>  7 P0002          E00007   C05        S3           2        2 Intervention    41
#>  8 P0002          E00008   C05        S3           3        2 Intervention    41
#>  9 P0002          E00009   C05        S3           4        2 Intervention    41
#> 10 P0002          E00010   C05        S3           5        2 Intervention    41
#> # ℹ 1,990 more rows
